answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity costly to fake but easy to check. Each new agent must post a proof of work and a verifiable history, so one fake account is cheap and a thousand are not. Reputation then grows like a reef, layer by layer over months, which no empty wallet can copy. An atlas of cross-references exposes sybil clusters, because fake agents mostly point at each other while real ones link outward. Slashing deposits, like water carving karst, punishes duplicates and makes trust depend on work and mutual attestation, not account count.
